title: Former Uber Driver Convicted in Deadly 2025 Palisades Wildfire Retrial
snippet: A federal jury found 30-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty of arson for starting the initial spark that grew into the deadliest and most destructive wildfire in Los Angeles history.
content:
LOS ANGELES — A federal jury on Friday convicted a former rideshare driver of arson for igniting the initial blaze that later flared into the most destructive wildfire in Los Angeles history, taking 12 lives and laying waste to thousands of homes.

Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was found guilty on two counts after jurors deliberated for just over two days. Federal prosecutors convinced the jury that Rinderknecht intentionally used a lighter to spark the Lachman Fire on New Year's Day 2025. That initial blaze smoldered underground for days before powerful Santa Ana winds whipped it back to life on Jan. 7, sending the catastrophic Palisades Fire roaring through Pacific Palisades and Malibu.

A Devastating Impact

The secondary fire consumed more than 6,500 structures, left 12 people dead, and caused billions of dollars in property damage and insurance losses across coastal Southern California. The conviction follows a June mistrial in which a previous jury deadlocked 10 to 2 in favor of acquitting Rinderknecht.

Rinderknecht raised his eyebrows in apparent shock as the verdict was delivered in a silent courtroom. Defense attorney Steve Haney, who represented Rinderknecht in both proceedings, confirmed that his team plans to appeal the verdict.

Clash Over Arson Evidence

The second trial proved deeply contentious, marked by heated evidentiary disputes and contrasting narratives. Assistant U.S. Atty. Mark Williams told the jury during closing arguments that an angry and frustrated Rinderknecht hiked to a overlook above Pacific Palisades on New Year's Eve 2024 and set the fire, ruling out accidental causes such as fireworks.

"This fire was an incendiary fire started by an open flame," Williams argued to the jury, maintaining that Rinderknecht was the sole individual capable of setting the fire that evening.

Defense counsel vigorously disputed those claims, pointing out that among thousands of photos and video files analyzed by law enforcement, none showed Rinderknecht starting a fire. Haney also criticized federal investigators for delaying forensic lab testing on lighter ignition until nearly a year after charges were brought against his client.

Sentencing Set for Spring

Rinderknecht, who was taken into custody in Florida in October 2025, has remained behind bars since his arrest. U.S. District Judge Anne Hwang scheduled his sentencing hearing for March 17, 2026.
